verses.text: Now these are the children of the province, who went up out of the captivity of those who had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, everyone to his city;
who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
The children of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two.
The children of Arah, seven hundred seventy-five.
The children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred twelve.
The children of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The children of Zattu, nine hundred forty-five.
The children of Zaccai, seven hundred sixty.
The children of Bani, six hundred forty-two.
The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty-three.
The children of Azgad, one thousand two hundred twenty-two.
The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-six.
The children of Bigvai, two thousand fifty-six.
The children of Adin, four hundred fifty-four.
The children of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight.
The children of Bezai, three hundred twenty-three.
The children of Jorah, one hundred twelve.
The children of Hashum, two hundred twenty-three.
The children of Gibbar, ninety-five.
The children of Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three.
The men of Netophah, fifty-six.
The men of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight.
The children of Azmaveth, forty-two.
The children of Kiriath Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three.
The children of Ramah and Geba, six hundred twenty-one.
The men of Michmas, one hundred twenty-two.
The men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred twenty-three.
The children of Nebo, fifty-two.
The children of Magbish, one hundred fifty-six.
The children of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The children of Harim, three hundred twenty.
The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-five.
The children of Jericho, three hundred forty-five.
The children of Senaah, three thousand six hundred thirty.
The priests: the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
The children of Immer, one thousand fifty-two.
The children of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
The children of Harim, one thousand seventeen.
The Levites: the children of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the children of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
The singers: the children of Asaph, one hundred twenty-eight.

The children of the porters: the children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, in all one hundred thirty-nine.
The temple servants: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth,
the children of Keros, the children of Siaha, the children of Padon,
the children of Lebanah, the children of Hagabah, the children of Akkub,
the children of Hagab, the children of Shamlai, the children of Hanan,
the children of Giddel, the children of Gahar, the children of Reaiah,
the children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda, the children of Gazzam,
the children of Uzza, the children of Paseah, the children of Besai,
the children of Asnah, the children of Meunim, the children of Nephisim,
the children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children of Harhur,
the children of Bazluth, the children of Mehida, the children of Harsha,
the children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children of Temah,
the children of Neziah, the children of Hatipha.
The children of Solomon’s servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Hassophereth, the children of Peruda,
the children of Jaalah, the children of Darkon, the children of Giddel,
the children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the children of Ami.
All the temple servants, and the children of Solomon’s servants, were three hundred ninety-two.
These were those who went up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer; but they could not show their fathers’ houses, and their offspring,  whether they were of Israel:
the children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda, six hundred fifty-two.

Of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Hakkoz, and the children of Barzillai, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name.
These sought their place among those who were registered by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they deemed disqualified and removed from the priesthood.
The governor told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to serve with Urim and with Thummim.
The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
besides their male servants and their female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and they had two hundred singing men and singing women.
Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five;
their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
Some of the heads of fathers’ households, when they came to Yahweh’s house which is in Jerusalem, offered willingly for God’s house to set it up in its place.
They gave according to their ability into the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold,  and five thousand minas  of silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.
So the priests, and the Levites, and some of the people, the singers, the porters, and the temple servants, lived in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

footnotes.content: Here begins the great return—not conquest, but homecoming. Those carried away as captives now walk back freely, each family to their own city. The Lord never forgets His scattered people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice Zerubbabel leads; beneath him stand Jeshua, Nehemiah, and ten others—witnesses and builders. Leadership rises not from force but from faithful remnant who stayed true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two thousand one hundred seventy-two from Parosh. Each number is a real family; each family carries real stories of exile and longing. The Lord counts His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three hundred seventy-two from Shephatiah—another lineage restored. The lists might sound dry, but they are a covenant kept: the God who called Abraham keeps His word to the smallest family.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven hundred seventy-five from Arah. In exile, they could have melted into Babylon, but they remembered their name, their tribe, their God. Exile tests faith—restoration proves it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two thousand eight hundred twelve from Pahathmoab, and the text names Jeshua and Joab—reminding us these aren't abstract groups but real lineages with real roots. Memory survives captivity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Elam sends one thousand two hundred fifty-four. How they must have walked—first through Babylon's streets, then toward home. Every step was answered prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nine hundred forty-five from Zattu. So many—each one choosing the hard road back instead of the comfortable life left behind. That's where true conversion lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zaccai sends seven hundred sixty. In those numbers, I see grandparents who whispered to grandchildren, 'We are going home to the God of our fathers.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bani: six hundred forty-two. The Lord's restoration gathers the humble, the ordinary, those whose names fill no history books—yet without them, there is no kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bebai sends six hundred twenty-three. Obscure families, unremarkable by the world's measure—yet the Lord knows every face, every heart, every choice to trust Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azgad's one thousand two hundred twenty-two were descended from royal line (see Ezra 10:15 for the name later), yet here they stand equal—no privilege in restoration, only faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adonikam brings six hundred sixty-six. This chapter's one unusual number—yet in the end, even the curious total matters. The Lord's math is always true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bigvai contributes two thousand fifty-six. One of the larger families—and their leader's name appears again in Ezra 10 as one who obeys hard reform. Numbers tell half the story; choices complete it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adin: four hundred fifty-four. In exile, small families had the hardest choice—pack the young and go, or try to build a life in a foreign land? These four hundred fifty-four chose the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ater of Hezekiah—ninety-eight. A smaller line, but the text honors them by naming the ancestor. Even the least are enfolded in God's covenant of return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bezai: three hundred twenty-three. Each family faced the same question: Does God truly call us home, or is this exile our end? Their answer, walking toward Jerusalem, says everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jorah: one hundred twelve. Smaller numbers matter just as much—each voice in the assembly, each hand to rebuild the altar, each heart that whispered 'Amen.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hashum brings two hundred twenty-three. Place by place, they arrive. The return isn't one grand moment but thousands of quiet, determined steps homeward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gibbar: ninety-five. Even tiny families matter in the Lord's accounting. He sees, He calls, He gathers—whether the number is large or small.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three—the very town where David was born, where Christ would later come. Now its children walk home to rebuild what exile tried to erase.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Netophah sends fifty-six. They remembered their place by name through seventy years of exile—that kind of faithfulness, that refusal to forget who they are, is where hope lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anathoth: one hundred twenty-eight. This was Jeremiah's hometown—the prophet who warned them of exile, and who lived to see the first glimmer of return. Faithful witness carries weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azmaveth: forty-two. A town that held steadfast through the long silence. Some places, like some people, prove their faith by simply enduring and remembering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three towns together—Kiriath Arim, Chephirah, Beeroth—seven hundred forty-three souls. Even in captivity, they kept their local ties, their neighborhood bonds. Community survives exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ramah and Geba: six hundred twenty-one. These were border towns, watching posts. Perhaps their people had seen more, endured more—now they lead in the return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Michmas: one hundred twenty-two. The geography of faith: each place listed is a thread in Israel's tapestry, and each thread is being woven back into the pattern.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bethel and Ai, two hundred twenty-three. Bethel, where Jacob dreamed of heaven; Ai, where Israel learned costly lessons. Both send their children home transformed by exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nebo: fifty-two. A smaller town, but every name is called; every one matters. The Lord doesn't rebuild kingdoms with the grand alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Magbish: one hundred fifty-six. Unfamiliar names, unknown stories—yet here they are, returned, ready to rebuild. Their obscurity doesn't diminish their place in God's plan.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The 'other Elam,' one thousand two hundred fifty-four—distinct from the first Elam (verse 7). The Lord divides and counts precisely; every branch of His people is known.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Harim: three hundred twenty. In the lists, each family is named, not numbered as mere units. Personhood, dignity, belonging—that's how the Lord sees His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lod, Hadid, Ono—three towns, seven hundred twenty-five people together. Geographic proximity echoes community. The Lord rebuilds not just individuals but woven families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jericho: three hundred forty-five. The city that fell at a whisper of faith in Joshua's day returns now with its descendants—not as conquerors, but as pilgrims seeking restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Senaah: three thousand six hundred thirty—by far the largest family in the chapter. Their size suggests influence, but all are equal here at the threshold of return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now come the priests—Jedaiah of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three. The priesthood returns to rebuild the altar first. Service to the Lord comes before comfort.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Immer's priests: one thousand fifty-two. These men carry the memory of sacrifice, of temple worship. In exile, they kept alive the hope of return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pashhur's line: one thousand two hundred forty-seven. Pashhur was a temple overseer; his descendants return to rebuild what he once oversaw. Responsibility spans generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Harim's priests: one thousand seventeen. Together, the four priestly families account for nearly five thousand souls. The Lord preserves His priesthood even in captivity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Levites—Jeshua and Kadmiel's line, seventy-four souls. Their number is small, but their role is essential: they serve in the house of God, in song, in intercession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The singers, Asaph's children: one hundred twenty-eight. Asaph was the psalmist of exile (see Psalm 73-83). His descendants return to restore the music of worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Porters—gatekeepers: one hundred thirty-nine combined. They guard the threshold, control access. Even this humble service is counted and celebrated in God's restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Temple servants, Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth—the work of the sanctuary needs many hands. These returning servants show that holiness requires faithfulness at every level.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: More temple servants: Keros, Siaha, Padon. Each name carries a story—likely descendants of foreigners who attached to Israel's faith. God's people have always been diverse.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub—the lists of servants grow. In exile, these families became strangers; now, returning, they reclaim their place in God's house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hagab, Shamlai, Hanan—each named, each recognized. Humility in service doesn't mean invisibility; the Lord sees and records.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah—ancient names, returning to an ancient land. Memory is the thread that stitches past to future.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam—more temple workers, more hands to sanctify the returning sanctuary. Multitudes make a kingdom; faithful service makes it holy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uzza, Paseah, Besai—the lists echo with purpose. These names are not decoration; they are the fabric of restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asnah, Meunim, Nephisim—servants whose families may have been originally foreign, yet they return to the God of Israel. Faith transcends ethnicity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur—in the returning community, there is room for all who serve. Hierarchy dissolves when the altar needs rebuilding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha—more workers, more families, more hope. The Lord restores not by heroic deeds but by the faithful gathering of ordinary people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Barkos, Sisera, Temah—Sisera was an ancient enemy name; now his descendants return as part of God's people. Even old enemies can become part of the family of faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Neziah, Hatipha—the list of temple servants closes. Together, they are the hands and hearts that keep God's house standing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Solomon's servants now return: Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda. Their ancestors served a king; now they serve the God who is King. Loyalty runs deep through generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jaalah, Darkon, Giddel—more of Solomon's household returning. A kingdom passes away, but God's household remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, Ami—the long list of servants closes. Each name deserves a place at the table of restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three hundred ninety-two—the total of all temple servants. They are neither priest nor Levite, yet without them, holiness cannot be maintained. All work matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some return from distant places—Tel Melah, Tel Harsha—and cannot prove their lineage. How humbling: to love God's people yet not know exactly where you belong. Yet the Lord calls them still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Delaiah, Tobiah, Nekoda—six hundred fifty-two who cannot show genealogy. They must trust in grace rather than pedigree. Faith doesn't require a bloodline.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Priests too face this test: Habaiah, Hakkoz, Barzillai's descendants cannot prove their lineage. One married into the Gileadite family and took their name. Even identity blurs in exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They are set aside from the priesthood—not from the people. The Lord is careful; holiness requires proof. Yet even in exclusion, there is mercy and place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The governor tells them to wait for a priest with Urim and Thummim—the tools of divine discernment. Decisions about God's people rest ultimately with Him, not human records.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty-two thousand three hundred sixty—the whole assembly. Imagine: more than forty thousand souls walking home after seventy years of exile. That is not chance; that is covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven servants, plus singers—male and female. Even the most humble have a voice in the returned community. The Lord hears all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven hundred thirty-six horses, two hundred forty-five mules. Animals for transport, for work, for dignity. The Lord provides not bare survival but restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four hundred thirty-five camels, six thousand seven hundred twenty donkeys. The sheer logistics speak: this is no small band, but a nation reborn, complete with all it needs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some heads of families offer willingly to rebuild God's house first, before their own. That is where the heart turns: toward the Lord, not toward comfort. Priorities reveal truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, one hundred priestly garments. They give 'according to their ability'—a principle that echoes through every faithful act. Generosity knows measure but not limit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse: the priests, Levites, singers, porters, servants—all Israel settled in their cities. As of 2026-10, we too are settled in cities small and large, yet the call remains the same: build God's house first, and all else finds its place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
